eli5.text: The server stopped printing messages into its activity log every time someone connects or disconnects from the realtime chat service. If you keep an eye on those logs, you will no longer see a line appear for each person joining or leaving, though the actual connecting and disconnecting still works exactly the same. This is already live and only affects people who read through those server logs.

ai.title: generateKnowledgeFiles reuses search system prompt for caching
ai.summary: generateKnowledgeFiles now calls getSearchSystemPrompt(fileContext) instead of manually composing getProjectFileTreePrompt and getRelevantFilesPrompt. The returned array is spread into the systemPrompt before appending the knowledgeFilesPrompt text block, aligning the prompt structure with the search agent. This change in backend/src/generate-knowledge-files.ts enables upstream prompt caching by matching the prefix used elsewhere. The fileContext data is injected via the shared search prompt builder rather than inline string interpolation.

eli5.text: When the assistant generates knowledge files about code changes, it now reuses the same setup prompt used by the search feature instead of building a custom one from scratch. This behind-the-scenes change aligns the two processes so that the prompt structure matches, allowing the system to cache and reuse prompt segments more efficiently. You won't notice any difference in the output, but it makes the backend slightly more consistent and faster. This is an internal refactor with no direct user-facing impact.

ai.title: Expand system prompt with tool call guidance and use cases
ai.summary: backend/src/system-prompt.ts updated to include explicit tool call syntax, purposes, and use cases for find_files and run_terminal_command. New manifold submodule added. This clarifies agent behavior for file discovery and terminal execution.

eli5.text: The assistant's instructions for how to find and read files, and how to run shell commands, were rewritten to be clearer and more detailed. A new section on using these tools was also added. These changes help the assistant behave more consistently and effectively when working with files and commands. The update is now live.

ai.title: Exclude tool results from last user message index
ai.summary: Fixes `lastUserMessageIndex` calculation in `main-prompt.ts` by filtering out messages containing `TOOL_RESULT_MARKER`. Previously, tool result messages (which have role 'user') were incorrectly identified as the last real user input, skewing `numAssistantMessages` counts and potentially affecting terminal call limits. This ensures the index points to the actual human prompt, not the agent's tool feedback loop.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant a question, a behind-the-scenes helper reads your chat to find the most recent message actually written by you. Previously, that helper could mistake the assistant's own tool feedback for your real question, which made it think you'd gotten fewer replies than you did and might cut off the conversation too soon. Now the helper skips over those internal tool notes, so it reliably stops at your genuine prompt. This only affects how the assistant tracks its own reply count, not anything you can directly see.

ai.title: Fix null handling in main-prompt test
ai.summary: Updated `processFileBlock` test to explicitly check for null results before destructuring. Prevents TypeScript errors and clarifies test intent. Scope limited to `test/__src__/main-prompt.test.ts`.

eli5.text: The assistant's internal instructions for handling files were cleaned up so they now check whether a file processing step actually produced a result before trying to use it. If an outside tool fails to return the expected file data, the assistant will no longer attempt to read from an empty or invalid response, which previously could cause a crash. This only affects how the assistant processes file attachments internally; you wouldn't see a visible new feature or setting, but it makes the handling of unsupported or broken file inputs more stable. The change is already live.

ai.title: Add placeholder comments to incomplete sketches in generate-patch
ai.summary: generatePatch now wraps incomplete sketches with `... existing code ...` placeholders when `shouldAddPlaceholderComments` is true. This prevents unintended deletions when Claude omits surrounding context in single-function edits. Changes affect `backend/src/generate-patch.ts` logic and `isSketchCompletePrompt` return structure.

eli5.text: When the code assistant makes a small edit to just one part of a file, it sometimes leaves out the rest of the file, which used to make the system accidentally delete the missing parts. The system now notices when the assistant did that and automatically marks the missing parts with a '... existing code...' label so they are preserved instead of being removed. This only affects single-edit requests and nothing changes for regular edits, but if you ever see that label in a suggested change, it means the surrounding code was intentionally kept intact.

ai.title: Add index file patch test case
ai.summary: Added test case 'should handle index file with placeholder at end' to `test/__src__/generate-patch.test.ts`. Includes mock data files (`expected.ts`, `new.ts`, `old.ts`) in `test/__mock-data__/index/` covering CLI entrypoint structure with `require.main` guard and `--help` handling. Test marked with `it.only` for focused execution.

eli5.text: A quality-check scenario was added to the project's test suite to confirm that a command-line startup file with a trailing placeholder is transformed correctly when generating patches. The developers who will notice are maintainers running these internal tests, and they'll see a new focused test case using example files that mimic the CLI entry script structure. This is live in the test code today, meaning the automated checks now cover this specific situation.

ai.title: Rename file XML tags to editfile across prompts and parser
ai.summary: The agent's file-editing XML tag changed from `<file>` to `<edit_file>` in all system prompts, diff-generation instructions, and the shared parser. This disambiguates edit blocks from other file references and aligns the CLI client's completion detection with the new tag. Updates span `backend/src/system-prompt.ts`, `main-prompt.ts`, `generate-diffs-prompt.ts`, `generate-diffs-via-expansion.ts`, `generate-knowledge-files.ts`, `common/src/util/file.ts`, and `npm-app/src/client.ts`. The regex patterns `fileRegex` and `fileWithNoPathRegex` now match `<edit_file ...>` instead of `<file ...>`, and the CLI waits for `- Editing file:` before announcing change application.

eli5.text: The assistant changed how it marks the parts of files it wants to modify during a coding task. Instead of wrapping each edit in simple `<file>` tags, it now uses `<edit_file>` tags. This makes it clearer which blocks describe edits versus ordinary file references, and it tells the assistant's companion tool to wait for the correct signal before announcing that a file change was applied. If you watched the assistant work, you'd see it now emit `<edit_file>` tags and wait for confirmation tied to those tags, rather than proceeding on a looser match. The change is live now.

ai.title: Move file changes status message to backend main-prompt
ai.summary: Moved 'Applying file changes. Please wait...' from client.ts to backend/src/main-prompt.ts. Backend emits via onResponseChunk when fileProcessingPromises.length > 0. Client.ts removes STOP_MARKER and '- Editing file: ' string-matching hack. CLI prints 'Complete!' after file list, and index.ts adds three init console.logs.

eli5.text: When the assistant starts applying file edits after answering you, a notice now appears that says 'Applying file changes. Please wait...' while the work happens behind the scenes. The text shows up the moment file editing begins, so you know changes are in progress instead of wondering why the response paused. You might also spot a short 'Complete!' line once the file list prints, plus a few friendly startup messages when the tool first loads.

eli5.text: The software was renumbered to 1.0.74, which bundles several small adjustments that make the assistant smarter and more reliable for anyone using it today. The assistant now receives clearer instructions on how to use its tools, handles file edits more cautiously by marking incomplete drafts, and shows more accurate timestamps when tracking which messages were last seen. You wouldn't notice the version number itself, but if you watched it work, file edits and message history would behave more consistently.
